content.text: In Zimbabwe, where PayPal and Stripe are heavily restricted, selling digital products like Notion templates to customers who prefer to pay with crypto has never been simpler. Notion's popularity has made template creators rich, but the traditional payment infrastructure has been a barrier to entry for many. The Sovereign Stack solves this problem by providing a fully sovereign digital commerce infrastructure that allows creators to collect payment in crypto without relying on Stripe or PayPal. With the Sovereign Blueprint, creators can deploy their own payment infrastructure in just 48 hours, giving them full control over their business and revenue streams.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters

The Sovereign Stack is a fully sovereign digital commerce infrastructure that allows creators to collect payment in crypto without relying on Stripe or PayPal. This means that creators can bypass the traditional payment processing fees and maintain full control over their business and revenue streams. The Sovereign Stack is built on top of GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments, which provides a secure and scalable payment processing solution that supports over 300 cryptocurrencies.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The Sovereign Stack architecture works by using GitHub Pages to host the website, Cloudflare Workers to handle backend logic, and NOWPayments to process payments. When a customer makes a purchase, NOWPayments automatically verifies the payment on the blockchain and triggers a webhook that sends the payment details to the creator's website. This allows the creator to deliver their digital product instantly, without relying on any intermediaries.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives or delivered via hosted video links, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase. Both approaches work reliably and cost nothing beyond the storage used.
Creators can deploy their own payment infrastructure in just 48 hours with the Sovereign Blueprint.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The Sovereign Stack consists of five key components: GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, NOWPayments, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. Each component plays a critical role in making the payment infrastructure work seamlessly together. By deploying these components, creators can build a fully sovereign digital commerce infrastructure that allows them to collect payment in crypto and deliver their digital products instantly.

Your Deployment Checklist

Prepare your product files in delivery-ready format — PDF for ebooks, ZIP archives for multi-file products, exported files for Notion templates, OTF and TTF archives for font families. Set your prices in USD and let NOWPayments handle the crypto equivalent calculation automatically at transaction time. Deploy your stack and configure the product list with file paths, USD prices, and delivery settings. Configure your storefront with product pages and checkout flow. Test the checkout on both desktop and mobile — confirm QR codes generate correctly and live price feeds display accurately. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link before the test download link expires. Check your order database and confirm the test transaction appears with all correct fields. Publish your store URL and review your first week of orders in the database to confirm the automated pipeline is running correctly.
